entries.title: Leviticus 2:1
segments: A meat-offering; meat, in the Bible, means any kind of food; in this case, it means flour, and articles of food made of it.  Of the burnt-offerings described in the preceding chapter, the whole was burnt with fire; of the meat-offerings described in this chapter, a part, called the memorial,
, was burnt, and the rest was eaten by the priests,

.  As the bloody offerings typified the expiation of sin through the blood of Christ, so these unbloody oblations signified that the offerer devoted himself and all that he had to God in holy love and obedience.  From such oblations the priests had, in part at least, their maintenance.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:2
segments: Oil--frankincense; emblems of the influences of the Holy Spirit, and the acceptable intercession of Christ and the supplications of his people.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:3
segments: God has ever required that a support be provided for his ministers. Under the Old Testament, he ordained that those who waited at the altar should be partakers with the altar; and under the New, that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:9
segments: Christ, as our great High-priest and Intercessor, must present all our offerings perfumed with the incense of his merits, in order to have them rise with acceptance before God.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:11
segments: No leaven, nor--honey; leaven was an emblem of hypocrisy, and honey of sensual indulgence, both of which are offensive to God.

entries.title: Leviticus 2:13
segments: Salt; an emblem of purity, integrity, and perpetuity.

Pride, hypocrisy, and sinful indulgence of every sort must be avoided, and humility, sincerity, and self-denial assiduously cultivated, if we would meet the approbation and obtain the blessing of the Most High.
